item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 162333
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Fri Oct 16 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Trudy, located a couple hundred miles southwest of Acapulco, Mexico,
and has issued the final advisory on the remnants of Simon, located
about one hundred miles southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form offshore of southern
Mexico during the early to middle part of next week. Environmental
conditions appear conducive for gradual development thereafter, and
a tropical depression is likely to form during the latter half of
next week while it moves generally westward to west-northwestward
over the eastern and central portions of the East Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Kelly

item.description:
Issued at 600 PM CST Fri Oct 16 2026 
000

BULLETIN
Hurricane Trudy Intermediate Advisory Number 14A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
600 PM CST Fri Oct 16 2026
 
...LITTLE CHANGE IN TRUDY'S STRENGTH OVER THE PAST FEW HOURS...
...TRUDY FORECAST TO APPROACH THE SOUTHWESTERN AND WEST-CENTRAL
COAST OF MEXICO THIS WEEKEND...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 600 PM CST...0000 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.0N 102.6W
ABOUT 220 MI...355 KM SW OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 300 MI...480 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...85 MPH...140 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 330 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...982 MB...29.00 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:

None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from Manzanillo northward to Cabo Corrientes
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from Manzanillo southward to Punta San Telmo
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from Manzanillo southward to Zihuatanejo
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico north of Cabo Corrientes to San Blas
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected 
somewhere within the warning area. A warning is typically issued 36 
hours before the anticipated first occurrence of 
tropical-storm-force winds, conditions that make outside 
preparations difficult or dangerous. Preparations to protect life 
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area. A watch is typically issued 48 hours before
the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force winds,
conditions that make outside preparations difficult or dangerous.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area within 36 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere in southwestern and west-central Mexico should
continue monitor the progress of Trudy. Additional watches or
warnings will likely be required tonight.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 600 PM CST (0000 UTC), the center of Hurricane Trudy was located 
near latitude 15.0 North, longitude 102.6 West. Trudy is moving 
toward the north-northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h). A 
north-northwestward to northwestward motion at a faster forward 
speed is forecast through Sunday. On the forecast track, the center 
of Trudy will approach the coast of southwestern and west-central 
Mexico on Saturday and pass near the coast Saturday night into 
Sunday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 85 mph (140 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Slight strengthening is possible Saturday and Saturday night.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140
miles (220 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 982 mb (29.00 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Trudy can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP1 and WMO header WTPZ41 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?key_messages.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are expected in the Hurricane Warning
area by late Saturday or Saturday night, with tropical storm
conditions spreading across the area on Saturday. Tropical storm
conditions are expected within the Tropical Storm Warning area by
late tonight or early Saturday. Hurricane conditions are possible in
the Hurricane Watch area by late Saturday, with tropical storm
conditions beginning on Saturday. Tropical storm conditions are
possible in the Tropical Storm Watch area on Sunday.
 
RAINFALL: Through the weekend, Trudy is expected to produce 4 to 8
inches with isolated higher totals around 15 inches along and near
the southwest Mexican coast in Michoacán, Colima and Jalisco. This
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides,
especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
Elsewhere, Trudy’s outer bands are expected to produce 2 to 4 inch
with isolated higher totals around 6 inches along the southwest
Mexican coast in Guerrero and Nayarit. This rainfall may result in
localized flash flooding through the weekend, especially in areas
along steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Trudy,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: Coastal flooding from storm surge is possible in areas
of onshore winds. Near the coast, the surge will be accompanied by
large and destructive waves.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Trudy are affecting portions of the coast 
of southwestern Mexico and will spread northward toward west-central 
Mexico during the next few days. These swells will cause 
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult 
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Gibbs

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 14
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Fri Oct 16 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 162041
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Trudy Discussion Number  14
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
300 PM CST Fri Oct 16 2026

After the last advisory was issued, the eye of Trudy disappeared and 
WFSM microwave data indicated that the central convective structure 
had decayed. In addition, a synthetic aperture radar overpass near 
12Z showed maximum winds of around 80 kt. When an Air Force Reserve 
Hurricane Hunter aircraft reached the storm between 18-19Z, it found 
a central pressure near 982 mb and maximum 700-mb flight-level winds 
of 76 kt. Based on this and satellite intensity estimates, the 
initial intensity has been reduced to 75 kt. The reasons for this 
weakening are speculative, but it one possibility is that the 
slow-moving hurricane has upwelled cold water underneath it as it 
crossed the paths of Polo and Rachel.

The initial motion is a somewhat erratic 330/4 kt. A gradual turn 
toward the northwest is likely during the next 12 hours or so as a 
weak low-level to mid-level ridge builds over eastern Mexico. This 
motion should continue through about 60 hours, with the center
passing near or possibly over the coast of west-central Mexico at 
about the 48-hour point. After that time, a weakening Trudy should 
be steered more by low-level flow, which should steer it generally 
west-northwestward. The new forecast track is near or just to the 
west of the previous track, and it lies a little to the right of 
the center of the guidance envelope.

Trudy's forecast track takes it into an area of deeper warm water, 
which in theory could cause the hurricane to re-intensify during 
the next 24 h or so. However, there still may be a tongue of dry 
air wrapping around the central core, and as the cyclone gets 
close to the coast of Mexico land interaction becomes a negative 
factor. Some of the guidance shows a little re-intensification, 
while some of it shows continued weakening. This part of the 
intensity forecast will include modest intensification during the 
first 24 h.  After 48 h, Trudy should encounter strong shear and a 
dry air mass, and this combination should produce steady weakening. 
The global models that keep the center offshore forecast the system 
to stop producing convection between 96-120 h, and the intensity 
forecast calls for the system to become a remnant low at that time. 
The new intensity forecast has major reductions in intensity 
compared to the previous forecast.
 
 
KEY MESSAGES:
 
1. While Trudy is no longer forecast to be a major hurricane when 
it approaches the coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico 
this weekend, it will still bring an increasing risk of storm surge, 
damaging winds, and flooding rain. Hurricane Warnings and Watches, 
as well as Tropical Storm Warnings and Watches, are currently in 
effect for portions of the coast, and additional watches and 
warnings will likely be required tonight.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Trudy will impact the southwest
Mexican coast between Guerrero and Jalisco through the weekend. This
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides by the
weekend along and near the southwest Mexican coast in Michoacán,
Colima, and Jalisco, especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
3. Large swells are affecting portions of the coast of southwestern
Mexico and will spread northward through the weekend, causing
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM MST (2100 UTC), the remnants of Simon were located near 
latitude 21.5 North, longitude 110.3 West. The remnants are moving 
toward the northwest near 13 mph (20 km/h).
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 35 mph (55 km/h) 
with higher gusts.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1006 mb (29.71 inches).

----------------------

Cyclone Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header

portions of the coast of west-central Mexico and Baja California Sur
during the next day or so. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
This is the last public advisory issued by the National Hurricane 
Center on this system. For additional information on the remnants of 
Simon please see High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather 
Service, under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN01 KWBC, and 
on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

item.title: Remnants of Simon Forecast Discussion Number 38
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Fri Oct 16 2026 
569 
WTPZ45 KNHC 162035
TCDEP5
 
Remnants Of Simon Discussion Number  38
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
200 PM MST Fri Oct 16 2026
 
Convection associated with Simon has rapidly diminished today. A 
recent scatterometer pass indicated that Simon no longer has a 
well-defined low-level center, and as a result, no longer meets the 
criteria for classification as a tropical cyclone. Therefore, this 
will be the final NHC advisory on Simon. The initial intensity is 
estimated at 30 kt.
 
The remnants are expected to move northwestward today, steered by 
the low- and mid-level flow between a trough to the west and a 
mid-level ridge to the northeast. This motion should keep the 
remnants moving parallel to the coast of Baja California Sur. 
Dissipation is expected by late tonight or early tomorrow morning.
 
For additional information on the remnants of Simon please see High 
Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service, under AWIPS 
header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN01 KWBC, and on the web at 
ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
